content.thinking:
Alright, the latest rebuild and test gave me a rather empty view of the TUI during a generation. After sending the 400‑word essay prompt, the capture after a few seconds only shows the status line and a single “Prisming…” line, then the prompt line again. That suggests the streaming area (the box that should be showing the generated text) is either not being updated correctly or is being overwritten/hidden.

What I need to verify is whether the streaming region is actually receiving data but not rendering, or if the data itself is getting corrupted or truncated. Since the UI uses a scrolling box that caps rows based on the terminal height, I suspect the overflow handling might still be off. The recent edits added an overflow="hidden" prop and a more sophisticated row budgeting based on column width, but I haven't actually looked at the middle of the pane during a generation—only the top and bottom lines.

The best way to inspect the middle of the pane is to capture a slice of the tmux pane output while the generation is in progress. I can let the generation run for a few seconds, then grab lines 5 through 22, which should correspond to the streaming box area (the first few rows are the prompt line and maybe some UI chrome). After that, I’ll also capture the very bottom four lines to confirm that the status line remains correct and that nothing weird is happening at the very end.

I’ll need a small pause before the capture so the generation has time to produce some content. Three seconds should be enough based on the previous runs (they showed some output after ~3 s). Then I’ll run `tmux capture-pane -t glint -p` and pipe it through `sed -n '5,22p'` to get the middle section. Immediately after, I’ll echo a marker and then use `tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | tail -4` to see the bottom lines (status line and prompt). This will give me a clear view of whether the streaming text is being rendered correctly or if there’s corruption.

Thus, the appropriate next action is a Bash tool call that sleeps 3 seconds, captures the pane slice, prints a separator, and then shows the bottom lines. This will let me diagnose the streaming region without further modifying code.

arguments.command: sleep 3; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | sed -n '5,22p'; echo "=== bottom ==="; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | tail -4
arguments.description: Check streaming region mid-generation for corruption
